demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson asks DocuMind no question: it reads counts, sizes and logs, and no read on this page depends on which store answers. The two windows below are on every page; you can skip both here, or pin acme now and put it back at the end if you want the UI's answers to come from the kit's index while you read. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.purpose: The chunk counts the lane recorded, document by document, before any arithmetic. Every size on this page starts from one number: how many chunks a document becomes. Your lane has already counted them, document by document, when the worker ingested the corpus. Read those counts first, in the browser, where an operator would. demos.heading: Measure the corpus with the kit's own chunker
demos.purpose: The averages the arithmetic multiplies, from the kit's code on the kit's files, in a second, with no network. The cell below loads every text document of the three tenants with shared/documind_corpus.py, the loader, chunker and batcher the notebooks share. They apply the worker's two rules, 2,000 characters with 200 of overlap and a section per ## heading, and the worker's two ceilings on a request. It counts, by document type, the characters, the chunks, the characters sent and the requests, then multiplies by 10,000,000. It reads only files in your clone of the kit: nothing on the lane, nothing billed.

demos.heading: REST: the index's own size
demos.purpose: The index's vectors, shards and shard size, and the deployment's machine and replicas, read from the Vertex AI API. make vector-status printed the fields gcloud was asked for. The API holds more: the index's shard size, its dimensions, and the deployed index's machine and replica range. The cell reads both with two GETs, then does the one sum that matters for sizing: how much of one shard your vectors fill.

demos.heading: Direct reads: Firestore's counts and the worker's seconds
demos.purpose: The rows the Firestore floor multiplies, and the one number no constant gives you: how long a document takes. Two reads finish the measurement. The first counts rows in Firestore without fetching them: a count() query returns one number instead of the rows it matched. chunk rows counts every version a tenant still holds: the current rows, and the rows a re-issue retired, which stay until their expire_at passes. current is what the index serves; added across the three tenants, it should match the index's vector count from steps 3 and 6. indexed sources is how many rows the fingerprint reads on every ingest to that tenant, which step 8 comes back to. Multiply your chunk rows by 59,092 bytes and you have your lane's Firestore floor for the chunks; for the 2,757 text chunks alone it is 155 MiB. At ten million documents it is 54.9 TiB. The second read is the calibration. Cloud Run logs every delivery Pub/Sub made to the worker, with its HTTP status and how long it took, so the median of those times is your lane's seconds per document. The cell saves the last month of deliveries, then counts them by status:
